methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective review of 618 pediatric acute leukemia patients over 20 years with an INSPPIRE-modified Atlanta criteria definition of AP. Comparisons use Fisher's/Mann-Whitney/Kruskal-Wallis and multivariable logistic regression with VIF checks. Strengths include the long horizon and explicit AP definition. However, only 17 AP cases severely limit statistical power, making the logistic regression with adjustment for age, sex, and protocol underpowered. The comparison of AP versus non-abdominal-pain controls mixes asymptomatic patients with those who had other abdominal diagnoses, and there is no adjustment for treatment era despite protocol changes from CCG (2004) through COG-adapted regimens (2024).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Identification of a cumulative L-asparaginase dose threshold (>=55,200 IU/m2) and high/very-high-risk protocol as AP risk factors is clinically actionable for monitoring and dose planning in Thai pediatric oncology centers. However, the threshold is novel and not externally validated, and the absence of genetic testing limits mechanistic and translational depth. This is a single-center retrospective cohort (effectively case series), Oxford LoE 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Setting, inclusion criteria, AP definition, protocols, variable definitions, and statistical plan are described with reasonable completeness, and CTCAE grading is explicitly defined. However, no STROBE checklist, no participant flow diagram, no data availability statement, and protocol-era breakdowns are not tabulated. The abstract is presented twice (one narrative, one structured), suggesting an editorial artifact. Reference 15 is attributed to Wondmeneh et al. but the CTCAE grading description is slightly incorrect (Grade 1 is not undefined in CTCAE v6.0 for pancreatitis).

novelty_literature.justification: AP as a complication of pediatric ALL treatment and its association with L-asparaginase dose is well-characterized (Wolthers 2017, Raja 2014, Chen 2022, Liu 2016). The specific cumulative dose threshold (>=55,200 IU/m2) is a quantitative refinement of prior thresholds (>45,000 U/m2/month in Chen 2022), and the Southern Thailand setting adds geographic context. Overall contribution is incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized clearly with numbered sections and readable discussion. Minor issues include duplicate abstract content, the unusual placement of sections under "Additional Sections", and some awkward phrasing ("most common within the first 6-10 months of treatment"). Tables and figures are well-referenced, but no figures are shown in the provided text.

key_strengths: Largest pediatric acute leukemia AP cohort reported from Southern Thailand (618 patients, 20 years)
Explicit INSPPIRE-modified Atlanta diagnostic criteria and CTCAE severity grading
Identification of a quantitative cumulative L-asparaginase dose threshold (>=55,200 IU/m2) with diagnostic characteristics (AUC 0.695, OR 5.25)
Clinically actionable finding that mortality is significantly higher in children with AP (76.5% vs 34.0%, p=0.005)
key_concerns: Only 17 AP cases limit power for multivariable modeling; confidence intervals for key ORs are wide (e.g., 5.25 [1.29-24.67])
No adjustment for treatment era despite protocol evolution from CCG-104/105/106 (2004) through COG-adapted regimens (2024)
No external validation of the 55,200 IU/m2 cutoff and no genetic susceptibility testing to contextualize the persistent-AP rechallenge case
Duplicate abstract, mislabeled CTCAE grade 1 definition, and absent STROBE flow diagram
Incremental contribution relative to established literature (Wolthers 2017, Liu 2016, Raja 2014)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Large single-center pediatric cohort with a clinically relevant dose-threshold finding, but low event counts and incremental novelty make mid-tier specialty publication appropriate after major revisions.
